turns.content: I'm 35, healthy, no regular medications. I take over-the-counter ibuprofen for headaches and it always upsets my stomach. Can I take it with food?

response:
Yes, taking ibuprofen with food or milk is one of the most effective ways to reduce the stomach upset it frequently causes. 

Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). These medications can irritate the stomach lining because they block substances in the body that normally help protect that lining from stomach acid. Having food in your stomach acts as a physical buffer and slows down the rate at which the medication contacts the stomach wall.

If you continue to experience stomach discomfort even when taking ibuprofen with food, or if you find yourself needing it frequently for headaches, it is a good idea to consult a doctor or pharmacist. They can help evaluate your headache triggers and recommend alternative pain relief options that might be gentler on your stomach.
